subject: Study design for density estimation with SMR - camera trap spacing

messages.author: 5c527e0ee4045a32
messages.subject: Study design for density estimation with SMR - camera trap spacing
parts:
Hello,


I’m hoping someone here can help me with a question. I am currently designing a camera trap study and plan to estimate density using an SMR model. I have read in multiple places that trap spacing should be no more than 2σ, however I am wondering how I know what the value of σ is. I understand it is somehow proportional to the radius of a home range, so if I have an average home range size for my study species can I calculate σ and use this to inform my trap spacing? 


Any guidance is much appreciated! 


Thank you,

Devin

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Study design for density estimation with SMR - camera trap spacing
parts:
1. σ  has varying meaning depending on the shape of the detection function. But let's not be pedantic, and assume you default to a halfnormal function on the probability (not hazard) scale ...
2. 2σ is not an upper limit, but rather a rough ballpark
3. Very approximately, halfnormal σ = sqrt(A/pi)/2.24 where A is 95% home range area. Better still, check literature on same or similar species
4. Use https://www.stats.otago.ac.nz/secrdesignapp/ (Spacing tab) to review the effect of spacing on precision (result depends on inputs not shown here).
5. Precision (relative standard error) is just one criterion. Also consider cost. And ensure representative sampling.
